title: Daily SGS Top 5
tagline: Five stories, one question: who's in control?

stories.headline: EU drops its hate-speech crime plan
stories.summary: The EU is dropping its plan to make hate speech an EU-wide crime. It never got all 27 nations to agree.
stories.label: Slightly Sovereign
stories.why: Each country keeps its own speech laws.
stories.what_it_means: Each country keeps its own speech laws, for now.
stories.economic_impact: Platforms avoid one more EU rulebook.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a neighborhood board dropping a porch rule, then writing a new mailbox rule.

stories.headline: Ottawa won't appeal Alberta's court win
stories.summary: Canada's government will not appeal Alberta's court win over the federal project-review law. Officials in Ottawa will rewrite the law instead, with no timeline yet.
stories.label: Moderately Sovereign
stories.why: Provinces get more say over projects.
stories.what_it_means: Provinces get more say over their own mines and pipelines.
stories.economic_impact: Investors still wait for the new rules.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a landlord who can't veto your kitchen.

stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Huang resigns
stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after admitting an affair. Finance chief Colette Kress is now interim CEO. Reports of a spy link are unconfirmed; China denies them, and the board sees no sign secrets were taken.
stories.label: Neutral
stories.what_it_means: The spy claim is still unproven.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a star coach quitting on an unproven scout report.

stories.headline: UK teen app ban could hit 150 apps
stories.summary: The UK's under-16 social media ban could grow to 150 apps. That includes YouTube Kids, Spotify and eBay.
stories.label: Moderately Globalist
stories.why: The government, not parents, picks the apps.
stories.what_it_means: The government, not parents, picks the apps, and everyone may face age checks.
stories.everyday_example: It's like banning kids from the whole mall because one store sells something bad.

stories.headline: Australia bill lets a regulator grab data
stories.summary: Australia's online safety bill would let a regulator collect political and religious data without consent, and share it with Ofcom and other overseas agencies.
stories.label: Strongly Globalist
stories.why: One official gets wide power to watch users.
stories.what_it_means: One unelected official gets wide power to watch users.
stories.economic_impact: Huge fines push platforms to take down too many posts.
stories.everyday_example: It's like the hall monitor mailing out everyone's diary.
